discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Quantum optics and superconducting quantum circuits
motivation: The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in Josephson circuits. Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf then took the next conceptual step. Their 2004 proposal and the experiment that followed it in the same year achieved strong coupling between a single superconducting qubit and a single microwave photon in an on-chip transmission-line resonator. This brought cavity QED into the solid state, with coupling strengths far beyond what atomic systems allow. Circuit QED gave the field dispersive quantum non-demolition readout, photon-number-resolved spectroscopy, bus-mediated two-qubit gates and the transmon. It also made bosonic error-correcting codes possible. Today it is the architecture behind essentially every superconducting quantum processor, including recent demonstrations of error correction below threshold. Beyond computing, it has opened new regimes of light–matter interaction and created quantum-limited sensors that are now used in searches for dark matter.
